attributes.action: More Training for GP's in regards to the deprescribing of Antidepressants.
attributes.additional_details: Approximately 8.8 million people take some form of psychiatric medication in the UK. This means statistically around 1.3 million will experience withdrawal, whether they know it or not. Doctors need to be made more aware of the Maudsley Deprescribing Guidelines and implementing properly calculated treatment plans for tapering off these medications to prevent long term harm to the patient.
attributes.background: More up to date guidance and training is needed for General Practitioners in the UK for deprescribing antidepressants. Many health care providers seem unaware of the physical and mental toll tapering an antidepressant can cause. There needs to be more adequate support and compassion shown.

rejection.details: The General Medical Council (GMC) is the regulator of all medical doctors, physician assistants (PAs) and physician assistants in anaesthesia (PAAs) (still legally known as anaesthesia associates and physician associates) practising in the UK. It sets and enforces the standards all doctors, PAs and PAAs must adhere to. The GMC is independent of Government, directly accountable to Parliament, and is responsible for operational matters concerning the discharge of its statutory duties.
